The game's great. I can't deny that. I love it, I've grown deeply attached to these goofy little ovals with circles on top, and have erased entire factions from planets for their sakes. The modding scene is incredibly diverse, the ost is amazing. But my main gripe is the cost of the DLC. You want the 5 content DLC that (mostly) revolutionize the game? That'll run you a mindboggling 160.75 AUD/111.88 USD/159.55 CAD (Exchange rates as of 8th October, 2026). This isn't even including the 44.95 AUD/31.28/44.62 CAD (Same as previous) required to buy the game itself. Shockingly enough, I feel that this is an absurd asking price for the full experience of [i] any [/i] game, no matter how incredible. Discounts are frequent, but small, ranging 10~20% at most, and only the already (relatively) inexpensive DLC get the large discounts.

[h1]THE BEST GAME IN THE WORLD[/h1]

I came across this game on pirate websites 12 years ago; after playing it for 45 hours over three days, I ended up opening Steam and buying it. Over the years, the mods created by the community and the extensive DLCs that have been added have meant that every year I’ve been able to play it again with a [u]brand-new theme[/u] and lose myself in it for hundreds of hours.

I’d like to mention a few of the themes and stories I’ve played through:

1- Following the Royalty DLC, I restricted all technological advancements in the game to the medieval era, filled the entire World with empires and factions. Then I've drew neighbouring settlements to my side through trade and diplomacy. I either assassinated the high-ranking leaders of factions I couldn’t reach an agreement with or conquered them by stationing catapults and mages at their borders. After hundreds of hours of strategy and resource management, I managed to unite the entire world under a single flag. The game had no end, [b][u]I was the one who wrote its purpose and adventure.[/u][/b]

2- Two years ago after the Anomaly DLC, I couldn’t find anything to satisfy my craving for Alien vs Predator, so I set up a gameplay experience entirely themed around the Alien franchise. I deployed my soldiers and medics onto the battlefield and equipped the entire area with turrets and patrols. I fought until I had eliminated every alien and anomaly presence in the surrounding area and my own sector. Unfortunately, after 100 hours, having lost all my men to facehuggers, this adventure came to a bitter end.

3- With the Biotech and Ideology DLCs, I wanted to design a peaceful playstyle utilising cutting-edge technology. With the Hospitality, caravans, advanced diplomacy and humanitarian aid type of mods, I exerted such a global influence that attacking others to establish dominance simply didn’t feel fair at all. My sole aim was to demonstrate my people’s superior ideology to everyone and lead them towards a better future. No weapon was lethal, and in my settlement -where there were far more medics than warriors- there was no room for failure. I would immediately transport the fallen to my state-of-the-art hospitals, produce new synthetic replacements for severed limbs, "impose" my ideology upon them, and release them back into the world. This was the first time I’d ever completed the game with its original ending.

There was also an automation-focused playstyle that I started entirely with androids where I've annihilated human populace and uploaded their consciousness to a virtual world, but if I were to start explaining that I’d end up writing another two or three paragraphs. 

[u]So in short:[/u] This is a game where you write the story yourself and can find exactly what you want to play right at your fingertips.

What’s more, with the 1.7 update, the game’s only downside *low FPS and slow loading time* has been improved massively, so what more can I say... This really is the BEST GAME IN THE WORLD.

Those who haven’t played it are missing out on a lot. The only thing I need to warn you about is this: Before you know it, whilst thinking "I’ll just play for another five minutes", you’ll find yourself seeing the first rays of the rising sun through the window. Don’t forget to get up and move about every hour, and just say "I can carry on tomorrow" and don't neglect real life ("It's time to Stop" mod is recommended). 

Lots of love to the awesome community, modders and Ludeon. Stay with RimWorld.

Si estas interesado en los dlcs pero no puedes comprar o conseguir todos de una/Solo piensas comprar Uno o dos en particular, recomiendo comprarlos en este orden:
1) Biotech, El mas importante, poder tener hijos, variantes geneticas, y los mechanitos (creo que se decia asi), personas que pueden controlar los robots llamados aqui 'Mechanoides'.
2) Ideology, Muy vital tambien, el poder de crear religiones, rituales, y un nuevo ending definitivo para la partida, muy bueno para formar partidas tematicas por como en base a la religion puedes crear la cultura de tu colonia.
3) Oddesey, Viaje planetario con aviones futuristas y poder ir a terrenos del cielo, un pseudo final (o evento de endgame importante) al que puedes llegar, pero uno que solo tiene todo su potencial si juegas biotech tmb.
4) Anomaly, Este se mezcla mejor con Ideology, basicamente añade Abnos a las que le puedes chupar energia como Lob corp y un sistema de investigacion, este es otro que tiene un pseudo final al que puedes llegar.
5) Royalty, el primer dlc, y ciertamente el menos importante, una nueva faccion, poderes psiquicos, y nuevas armas que se vinculan con tus colonos, eso suena mas interesante de lo que realmente es, añade un nuevo final, pero entre los otros es ciertamente el mas debil.

El juego en si mismo es uno bastante caro pero si sabes que volveras y seguiras jugandolo como loco montones de veces, adelante y disfrute, ya sea de la vida chill, o de pelear el dia a dia pensando como se aguantara para mañana. Good luck on the Rim.

Ludeon has become far too greedy, completely fragmenting the gameplay experience in favor of increasingly blatant greed with a constant stream of DLCs, each seemingly more expensive and less relevant than the last, with prices now approaching that of the base game itself. 

And yet, the base game still has huge shortcomings that have never been addressed. 
Most of the mechanics of the base game and the DLCs are lazily implemented and clearly rely on mods to flesh them out.

You  mine steel and electronic components straight out of the mountain (??), yet a DLC adds car wrecks into the environnement, that still serve absolutely no purpose...

It's almost impossible to interact with visitors, even when they're the lost siblings, parents, or children of your own colonists. They show up, wander around for a while, and leave without anything happening or any way to interact with them. You really have to wonder what the point is. At times, the game genuinely feels unfinished.

The world is massive, but desperately empty. In reality, almost nothing interesting ever happens in the world around you and nothing makes you want to explore it. 

The "storytellers" are mostly smoke and mirrors: behind the fancy name, they're really just different difficulty settings that don't actually change the story being told, but just spam more or less of the always exact same few events. 

Breeding animals is a micromanagement feast.
Diseases just pop randomly on a random number of random colonists, regardless what they were doing at that moment, and never propagate. Actually, most events work the same way. They just pop randomly and for no reason.
A father would kill his own daughter with his bare hands over a "social fight" because he ate without a chair.

All this, I could forgive when Rimworld was a single dev game struggling to add content, but after 5 DLC, each more expensive and pointless then the previous one, and spending $150 into the game, I cannot just forgive this anymore. 

Because the worst part is that the 100+ bucks worth of DLCs don't even fix these issues. They just add more content, often a mishmash of unrelated features with little to no real coherence between expansions. The DLCs don't add lore, they just dilute it into an irrelevant and souless mess that sometimes contradicts itself. 
Some extension don't really work good with each other and I had to disable some features or extensions to have a coherent and pleasant gameplay. 
 Features that genuinely make the game deeper, more coherent, and more interesting, such as events, genetics, or cultural systems, are locked behind paid expansions, further fragmenting the experience between players without any overarching vision, all while the base game continues to sell millions of copies, just as it did at its peak.

If I've put 800 hours into this game, it's entirely thanks to the modding community, whose members are the only ones who've bothered to address all these shortcomings for free, while Ludeon was busy releasing another $25 DLC, plushies, T-Shirts, totbags and ugly $15 pins.
I don't want to be milked anymore. 

At this point, I can no longer recommend RimWorld; because the base game is too shallow, and the full experience is not worth $150. 

At this point, I'd rather recommend looking into other indie developers with a much better attitude toward their own games.

I've never seen a community like this one, and the Workshop page is honestly breathtaking. I've been here since before the Royalty DLC and have watched the game grow. The developers are awesome, and every update and DLC is great. The game and its DLCs rarely go on deep sales, though, and the DLCs are basically mandatory if you want limitless gameplay and mods, so prepare your wallet. It's all worth your money, though.

I'd suggest getting the Biotech DLC at least, then Ideology/Odyssey > Royalty > Anomaly. Personally, I can't imagine a run without Biotech and Royalty. Royalty was the first DLC released and is the smallest, but with the Vanilla Psycasts Expanded mod, it's gotta be one of the most fun. Biotech expands on many areas and comes in handy for every type of run. Ideology is a nice way to change up your gameplay even without mods; mostly, it's either a roleplay-type run where you shoot yourself in both kneecaps to play by specific rules, or you make an overpowered religion or cult. Nowadays, I find myself playing without it as I've tried so many combinations already. Odyssey is a huge expansion where, depending on your run, you might not really come across a lot of its features unless you devote your run to it, so it might not be the best starter DLC. Anomaly is... well, it's interesting, but you won't really miss out on anything by not getting it. If you don't make a whole run about it, it's like it's not even there—you might do two or three runs with it and tuck it away forever.

Thank you for reading this. If you did, just buy the game already and go rimming.

Side note: Load times with a huge mod list can be a bit longer. What I found is that it loaded faster for me with the same mod list on CachyOS compared to Win10. So for all the Linux enthusiasts out there: it runs better on Linux!

I just read the Waylith Engine announcement and holy shit, Ludeon, what are you guys cooking?

A new engine for RimWorld, supposedly 2–4x better performance, and they managed to keep existing saves and most of the modding ecosystem working?

HOW DOES THAT EVEN WORK??

This is RimWorld we're talking about. A game where people have hundreds of mods installed, and somehow the whole thing still runs. Replacing the engine without breaking everything sounds like a nightmare on its own, let alone pulling it off while keeping the game we all know and love.

And the best part? They're doing this for a game that's already been around for years. No RimWorld 2, no starting from scratch, no making everyone buy the same game again. Just making the original better.

Honestly, huge respect to Ludeon Studios. You don't see this kind of dedication every day. RimWorld was already one of my all-time favorite games, but stuff like this makes me appreciate it even more.

Rimworld is one of the greatest games ever made. It has so much detail, content, and replayability. You can do pretty much whatever you want, and the game, while difficult, and sometimes unfair, never gets stale.

The game has a blend of gritty realism and "rule of cool" gameplay mechanics. A small wound can make your colonist bleed out or get infected, and your colonist may die due to health complications regarding the injury. Meanwhile another colonist could get mauled by a terminid straight out of 40K, lose all their limbs and half their organs and miraculously survive and be turned into a cyborg if you have the capabilities. 

Anything can and will happen; and the awesome AI (not thgat kind of AI) game director will keep you on your toes and keep things spicy and interesting without overwhelming you all the time. 

You will get raided, you will starve, your entire colony will be obliterated by catastrophically stupid mistakes you make on your part, but that's the fun of the game. Do whatever you can for your precious colonists, and get atatched to them, then lose them in horrific accidents. That's the game. It's brutal and morbid, but also fun as all hell.

Rimworld is also super well optimized and stable. You can play the game on practically anything. Also the game's community is awesome and there is a vast modding scene.

The DLC is pretty cool too but is absolutely not required for the base game to be worth it and fun. It's just extra.

TLDR: Worth the price, absolute masterpiece
